applicant_utility.summary: The income test is the feature that catches people out: a Gross Monthly Household Income above S$15,000 at the point of admission disqualifies you regardless of results, and the threshold is measured on total household income including overtime pay, allowances, cash awards, commissions and bonuses. You must already be a local polytechnic graduate or final-year student aiming at an overseas STEM degree, so JC and A-Level applicants are outside this scheme entirely. Nothing on the page publishes a monetary value, so the offer is worth what the named components add up to rather than a headline figure, and the 4-year bond in a STEM role is the price of it.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Singapore Citizen polytechnic graduates or final-year polytechnic students from households at or below S$15,000 gross monthly income, heading to an overseas STEM degree.
application_readiness_checklist: Calculate household income against Temasek's definition, which counts basic employment income, trade or self-employed income, overtime pay, allowances, cash awards, commissions and bonuses.
Confirm the target course is STEM and is not Medicine or Dentistry before investing in overseas applications.
Merge every supporting document into one file before you start, because the CV submission is a single upload.
Check whether you are enlisting for National Service; Temasek explicitly allows those applicants to apply.
Use preliminary polytechnic diploma results if finals are not out yet, since the application does not require them.
common_rejection_risks: Household income creeping above S$15,000 by the point of admission, even if it was below the threshold at application.
Applying as a JC or A-Level holder rather than a polytechnic graduate or final-year polytechnic student.
Naming Medicine or Dentistry, which are excluded from the STEM course eligibility.
Not being accepted into an overseas university, since the provisional offer is conditional on it.
Assuming a full monetary value from the benefit list, which carries no figures at all.
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Temasek publishes no amounts for tuition, the living allowance, relocation, pre-studies or application fees, so the uncovered gap cannot be quantified from the official page; anything outside the named components is self-funded.
document_audit: Everything goes into one consolidated file under CV submission, so file order and completeness matter more than separate attachments.
University application and outcomes are only 'if available', so an incomplete overseas application does not block submission.
Preliminary polytechnic diploma results are acceptable, which removes the excuse of waiting for finals.
The household income declaration is made in the application itself, so the declaration and any supporting evidence should be consistent.
alerts: The AY2026/2027 window was extended to 15 September 2026 and the page still advertises it as open, so watch for the AY2027/2028 window rather than trusting the banner.
Assessment is four stages deep: psychometric and personality assessment, remote on-demand video interview, a full-day in-person group assessment, then a 60-minute structured interview.
The 4-year bond requires a STEM-related role in Singapore or with a Singapore-headquartered company, which also constrains postgraduate plans.
Offer confirmation waits on final cumulative GPA, exam results and an overseas university acceptance, so even a strong application can still fall through.
This is an overseas-study award; a local polytechnic-to-local-degree plan is covered by the sibling Temasek Undergraduate Local Scholarship instead.
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Single-file Brightsparks application with the household income declaration, then four assessment stages, then a provisional offer conditional on final results and an overseas acceptance.
